# Risk Register Archive

Last updated: 2026-07-11

This archive tracks product, correctness, security, and project risks observed
from public source review. It is intentionally biased toward fail-fast behavior:
when an adapter or extension cannot provide the documented semantics, active-ts
should report that clearly instead of returning approximate or silently partial
results.

The current active-risk dashboard lives in [risk-register.md](risk-register.md).
This file keeps the full historical audit log so the dashboard stays readable.

## Scoring

| Field | Values |
| --- | --- |
| Priority | P0 = correctness or data-safety risk, P1 = important reliability/design risk, P2 = maturity or adoption risk |
| Likelihood | Low, Medium, High |
| Impact | Low, Medium, High, Critical |
| Status | Open, In Progress, Mitigated, Accepted |

## Register

| ID | Priority | Risk | Evidence / trigger | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R-001 | P0 | Bound model APIs may ignore `Model.use(context)` | Static methods such as `find`, `query`, `where`, `search`, and aggregate helpers still rely on the default context. A class returned from `Model.use(context)` can therefore bind only construction, not static reads/writes. | High: request-scoped context, tests, and multi-app usage can hit the wrong adapters. | High | Static methods now route through bound model context metadata, with tests for bound reads and creates. | Mitigated |
| R-002 | P0 | Negative cache semantics do not match metadata | `EntityOptions.cache.negativeTtl` exists, but missing rows can be cached with the normal TTL. `create` does not currently guarantee invalidation of an earlier cached miss. | High: a row created after a cache miss can continue to read as `null` until TTL expiry. | High | Positive and negative cache writes use separate TTLs, and create/update/delete invalidation clears stale misses. | Mitigated |
| R-003 | P0 | One-to-one relation loading can ignore `foreignKey` | `RelationMeta` includes `localKey` and `foreignKey`, but one relation loading can treat `owner[localKey]` as the target id. | High: relations with non-id foreign keys can return the wrong row. | Medium | One relations query by `foreignKey` when it differs from the target id field, with coverage for non-id foreign keys. | Mitigated |
| R-004 | P0 | Relation `preload` metadata is not yet a real loading plan | `preload` appears in metadata/docs, but relation loading does not consistently translate it into `select()` or nested include behavior. | Medium: users can expect RTT or projection optimization that does not occur. | High | Relation preload is applied as a select projection for lazy and batched relation queries, including target id and foreign key fields required for matching. | Mitigated |
| R-005 | P0 | `SearchBuilder.where()` may be silently ignored or adapter-specific | `SearchOptions.where` is exposed, but built-in search adapters do not have a clearly uniform filter contract. | High: users can receive unfiltered search results while believing filters were applied. | High | Memory search applies `where`; other built-in adapters declare unsupported filters and fail fast instead of ignoring them. | Mitigated |
| R-006 | P0 | Query semantics differ across store adapters | `orWhere`, `contains`, `startsWith`, range comparisons, nested fields, and numeric comparisons can differ by adapter. Some backends may approximate unsupported operators. | Critical: the same query can return different data depending on backend. | High | Store capability declarations, fail-fast planning, direct adapter rejections, and expanded contract coverage now cover OR groups, startsWith, explicit containment operators, nested fields, numeric comparisons, aggregates, cursor smoke tests, and typed ids. | Mitigated |
| R-007 | P0 | Prefix search can degrade to broad range search | Firestore/Datastore-style `startsWith` implementations can become `>= prefix` without an upper bound. | High: prefix queries can include unrelated rows larger than the prefix. | Medium | Adapters that cannot express safe prefix semantics now declare `startsWith: false`, causing the planner to reject the query. | Mitigated |
| R-008 | P0 | PostgreSQL JSON numeric comparisons can behave like string comparisons | JSON `#>>` extracts text; range comparisons and ordering can be lexicographic unless explicitly cast based on field type or query intent. | High: numeric filters and sort order can be wrong. | Medium | Models can declare field types; PostgreSQL casts numeric field filters and ordering to `double precision`, and numeric range filters infer numeric casting from numeric operands. | Mitigated |
| R-009 | P1 | `select()` result shape is not standardized | Some adapters include id automatically, some may ignore projections, and dotted paths can be returned as literal keys instead of nested objects. | High: partial selections can break model validation, ids, and relation loading. | Medium | `select()` now returns partial model instances, always includes the id field, bypasses full read validation for partial rows, blocks full-model operations on partial instances, and has memory/MongoDB/Firestore/Datastore projection coverage. | Mitigated |
| R-010 | P1 | String and number ids can collide internally | `EntityId` is `string | number`, while cache/batch/memory keys commonly use `String(id)`. `1` and `"1"` can become the same internal key. | High: cross-row contamination in cache, batch loads, or memory tests. | Medium | Internal, built-in store storage, and built-in search document ids now use the typed id codec, with contract coverage for numeric `1` vs string `"1"`. | Mitigated |
| R-011 | P1 | Transaction implementation can mutate shared context state | Transaction routing currently swaps store state on the active context. Shared contexts across concurrent requests/tests can leak transaction stores or queues. | Critical in concurrent services; Medium in single-threaded tests. | Medium | Transactions now execute in forked child contexts instead of mutating the parent store map. | Mitigated |
| R-012 | P1 | Metadata cache can become stale after late metadata mutation | Resolved metadata is cached in `ActiveContext`. Late `defineModel().attach()` or decorator/static schema application can leave existing contexts with old metadata. | High: indexes, relations, hooks, codecs, and scopes can differ by context timing. | Medium | Model metadata now tracks versions, invalidates resolved cache entries, and dedupes indexes/search indexes on attach. | Mitigated |
| R-013 | P1 | Search indexing lifecycle is incomplete | Search adapters expose indexing APIs and hooks include index events, but core create/update/delete does not automatically sync search indexes. | Medium: search appears configured but can stay stale unless app code indexes manually. | High | Outbox search sync worker support is available for idempotent index/delete processing. | Mitigated |
| R-014 | P1 | Adapter capability matrix is missing | Query planner and contracts do not yet have a first-class `supports` declaration for each adapter. | High: unsupported behavior can be approximate or invisible. | High | Store and search adapters now expose capabilities and the context validates query/search plans before execution. | Mitigated |
| R-015 | P1 | Cursor pagination is not standardized | `QueryPlan.cursor` exists, but adapter cursor formats and order requirements are not unified. | Medium: production pagination can duplicate or skip rows across adapters. | Medium | active-ts store cursor support is standardized on the core keyset cursor codec with stable id tie-breakers. Memory supports it; adapters with native opaque cursors now declare unsupported until they can map to the standard contract. | Mitigated |
| R-016 | P2 | Nested include and relation preloading are shallow | Current include behavior is relation-name oriented and does not support deep include plans such as `posts.comments.author`. | Medium: complex object graph loading can regress to N+1 patterns. | Medium | Include supports dotted paths and object notation, and list queries batch one/many foreign-key relation preloads via shared `in` queries while preserving nested includes. | Mitigated |
| R-017 | P2 | Soft delete/default scope is not built in | Apps commonly need `deletedAt = null`, restore, and with-deleted controls. | Medium: every app reimplements deletion semantics differently. | Medium | The soft-delete plugin provides default query/aggregate scoping plus `softDelete()`, `restore()`, `withDeleted()`, and `onlyDeleted()` helpers. | Mitigated |
| R-018 | P2 | Optimistic locking is not available | Concurrent saves can overwrite each other unless the app implements version checks externally. | Medium to High depending on workload. | Medium | Version-field saves now call adapter conditional updates. Memory, MongoDB, and PostgreSQL implement compare-and-set writes; unsupported adapters fail fast. | Mitigated |
| R-019 | P2 | Schema migration CLI is missing | Schema plans exist, but developers do not yet have `diff`, `generate`, or `apply` commands. | Medium: schema management remains manual and adoption friction grows. | Medium | `active-ts schema diff`, `schema generate`, and `schema apply` are implemented. | Mitigated |
| R-020 | P2 | Cache policy needs production hardening | Tenant-aware keying, stale-while-revalidate, stampede prevention, per-query cache policy, and negative TTL separation are not fully developed. | Medium: high-traffic services can suffer stale reads or cache stampedes. | Medium | Entity cache keys support context-level resolvers, function caches support namespaces and stale-while-revalidate, and existing negative TTL plus singleflight coverage remains in place. | Mitigated |
| R-021 | P2 | Validation adapters are narrow | The public story is typia-compatible validators, but many TypeScript projects use Zod, Valibot, or ArkType. | Low to Medium: adoption friction rather than correctness. | Medium | Typia, Zod, Valibot, and ArkType-style validators can be normalized through adapter helpers. | Mitigated |
| R-022 | P2 | Open-source release readiness is incomplete | README says no license has been selected and SECURITY notes no private vulnerability channel. CI/release workflow also needs to be visible. | High for public adoption and legal clarity. | High | MIT license, CI, release workflow, packaged metadata, and GitHub Security Advisory reporting are documented. | Mitigated |
| R-023 | P0 | Datastore declared indexes can be excluded from indexes | The Datastore adapter sent `model.indexes.flatMap(fields)` as `excludeFromIndexes`, reversing the meaning of declared indexes. | High: fields intended for query/order can be excluded from Datastore indexes. | High | Removed automatic `excludeFromIndexes` generation from declared indexes; future exclusion should use dedicated metadata. | Mitigated |
| R-024 | P0 | `orWhere()` can weaken security scopes | A tenant or visibility predicate in the base `where()` branch can be bypassed by a broad OR branch if treated as an ordinary filter. | Critical: multi-tenant data exposure. | Medium | Chaining `where().orWhere()` now fails fast. Use explicit `whereAny()` groups; prior `where()` and named `scope()` predicates are copied into every OR branch as global constraints. | Mitigated |
| R-025 | P1 | PostgreSQL `contains` differs from memory semantics | Memory treats `contains` as array membership or string substring, while PostgreSQL JSON text extraction plus `LIKE` can produce false positives. | High: adapter-specific query results. | Medium | Portable code should use explicit `arrayContains`, `textContains`, and `jsonContains` operators. PostgreSQL does not advertise portable containment and direct adapter calls fail fast; native SQL remains available for backend-specific containment. | Mitigated |
| R-026 | P1 | Native search can bypass underlying store capabilities | The native search adapter builds store `contains`/OR queries internally, outside `ActiveContext.searchAdapterFor()` capability validation. | High: unsupported search can silently broaden or fail late. | Medium | Native search now checks underlying store `textContains`, OR, and cursor capabilities at execution and returns empty results when no search fields are configured. | Mitigated |
| R-027 | P1 | Search document ids can collide by id type | Algolia used `${model}:${String(id)}` and Elasticsearch used `String(id)`, so `1` and `"1"` could target the same search document. | High: search index contamination. | Medium | Algolia and Elasticsearch now use the typed id codec for document ids, and Elasticsearch preserves or restores the model id field from hits. | Mitigated |
| R-028 | P1 | Adapter contract suite is too shallow | Contract tests covered basic create/get/query/update/delete but not projection, OR, aggregate, cursor, or typed id collisions. | Medium: adapter regressions can pass the suite. | High | Store adapter contracts now include typed id collision, projection id inclusion, OR behavior, startsWith, array/text/json containment, nested fields, aggregates, cursor follow-up pages, and safe schema coverage when supported. | Mitigated |
| R-029 | P0 | Store middleware can drop optimistic-lock write options | Middleware wrappers can accept only `(model, id, data)` and call the wrapped adapter without `StoreWriteOptions.expectedVersion`. | Critical: wrapping a store can silently disable version CAS. | Medium | Store middleware forwards `StoreWriteOptions`, exposes them in middleware args, and tests verify expectedVersion reaches the wrapped adapter. | Mitigated |
| R-030 | P0 | Partial projection models can replace full rows | `select()` produces a model instance, and calling `save()` on it can full-replace data with only projected fields. | Critical: non-selected fields can be deleted. | High | Partial instances are marked internally and full-model operations such as `save()`, `include()`, `ref()`, views, and policies fail fast. | Mitigated |
| R-031 | P1 | Optimistic locking can be assumed when capability is missing | `Model.save()` can treat an undefined `optimisticLock` capability as support and pass `expectedVersion` to custom adapters. | High: custom adapters can ignore expectedVersion while appearing safe. | Medium | Versioned saves now require `capabilities.optimisticLock === true`; false or omitted support fails fast. | Mitigated |
| R-032 | P1 | Memory search can search fields not declared in search indexes | Test-only memory search can search the entire JSON document while production adapters search declared fields. | Medium: tests can pass for searches production adapters would not match. | High | Memory search now searches only declared `searchIndexes` fields and returns empty results when no search fields are configured. | Mitigated |
| R-033 | P1 | Search sync worker can use incomplete model metadata | The worker can reconstruct minimal metadata with `idField: 'id'` and no search indexes/codecs. | High: custom id fields, codecs, or field-based search adapters can break. | Medium | `runSearchSyncWorker()` accepts an active context and uses `context.meta(model)` for resolved metadata, while keeping legacy fallback for old callers. | Mitigated |
| R-034 | P2 | Portable `contains` operator is ambiguous | A single `contains` name can mean array membership, text substring, or JSON containment depending on adapter. | Medium: adapter contracts and user expectations remain unclear. | Medium | The legacy `contains` operator now fails fast. Portable code must use explicit `arrayContains`, `textContains`, and `jsonContains` operators. | Mitigated |
| R-035 | P0 | Search sync can lose drained outbox events on adapter failure | `runSearchSyncWorker()` drains events before indexing them. If search indexing fails after the drain, undelivered events can disappear. | High: search indexes can permanently miss writes unless another repair job exists. | Medium | The worker requeues the failed and undelivered events before rethrowing, and tests cover retry after a search adapter failure. | Mitigated |
| R-036 | P0 | `create()` duplicate-id semantics differ by store adapter | Memory can overwrite existing rows, Datastore `save()` is upsert-like, and MongoDB can insert duplicate documents unless the model id is uniquely enforced. | High: tests can hide duplicate create bugs or production adapters can diverge. | Medium | Memory create now conflicts on existing ids, Datastore uses insert-only when available, MongoDB stores typed ids in `_id`, and the shared contract verifies duplicate create rejection. | Mitigated |
| R-037 | P0 | Transaction reads can observe stale shared cache after writes | Cache invalidation is deferred until commit, so a transaction can update/create a row and then re-read an older positive or negative cache entry before commit. | High: business logic inside a transaction can make decisions from stale data. | Medium | Transaction state now tracks dirty cache keys, bypasses shared cache reads and writes for those keys, and still defers shared invalidation until commit. | Mitigated |
| R-038 | P0 | Transactions can run on non-transactional stores | `context.transaction()` can execute the callback without a real store transaction when the selected adapter lacks `transaction`. | Critical: callers can believe writes are atomic when they are not. | Medium | The context now fails fast when the selected store has no transaction implementation. | Mitigated |
| R-039 | P0 | Cross-store writes inside a transaction are not atomic | A transaction scoped to one store can still write to another registered store through the same child context. | Critical: partial commits across stores can leave inconsistent state. | Medium | Transaction child contexts wrap non-selected stores as read-only guards and reject create/update/delete with a clear error. | Mitigated |
| R-040 | P1 | Function cache can resolve different keys for one computed value | `get()` resolves a key and `compute()` can call `set()`, which resolves async key/namespace functions a second time. | High: side-effectful or time-varying key resolvers can write under a different key than the miss being filled. | Medium | Computed values are written through the already resolved key, and regression tests assert async key/namespace resolvers are called once per miss. | Mitigated |
| R-041 | P0 | Hooks can mutate query plans after validation | `beforeQuery` and `beforeAggregate` hooks receive compiled plans and can inject unsafe fields, operators, sort specs, or aggregate fields that custom adapters may trust. | High: unsafe adapter inputs or inconsistent validation between hook and adapter paths. | Medium | Query, aggregate, and search options are sanitized again after hooks and before adapter routing/execution. | Mitigated |
| R-042 | P1 | Relation names can use reserved object keys | `defineModel().ref()` and `hasMany()` validate relation key fields but not the relation name itself. | Medium: reserved names such as `__proto__` or `constructor` can enter metadata and confuse relation lookup. | Medium | Relation names are validated through the same safe field-path guard as other metadata names. | Mitigated |
| R-043 | P1 | Algolia cursor parsing is too permissive | `Number(cursor) || 0` treats invalid or negative cursor values as page `0`. | Medium: malformed cursors can silently restart pagination. | Medium | Algolia cursors now require unsigned safe-integer page strings and reject malformed cursors. | Mitigated |
| R-044 | P1 | PostgreSQL index names can collide across tables | Schema apply uses the raw model index name, so two tables with `lookup` can share a schema-global index identifier. | Medium: schema sync can skip required indexes or fail depending on table order. | Medium | PostgreSQL schema apply namespaces index identifiers with the model/table name and tests same-name indexes across models. | Mitigated |
| R-045 | P1 | Memory transactions expose uncommitted writes | The memory adapter previously executed transaction callbacks against the parent store instance and restored from a snapshot only on rollback. | High: tests using parent and transaction contexts concurrently can observe rows before commit. | Medium | Memory transactions now execute against an isolated transaction store and apply dirty writes to the parent only after commit. | Mitigated |
| R-046 | P1 | Memory adapters can return live object references | Direct memory store/cache/search reads can return the stored object itself. Mutating the returned value can mutate persisted test state. | Medium: tests can pass or fail based on accidental aliasing that real DB/cache adapters would not expose. | High | Memory store, cache, and search adapters now clone values at read/write boundaries, with direct adapter regression coverage. | Mitigated |
| R-047 | P1 | Lazy relation loading can ignore nested `localKey` paths | Batched include loading uses safe path resolution, but direct lazy relation loading can read `owner.data[localKey]` literally. | Medium: relations with `localKey: 'profile.accountId'` can return `null` unless loaded through include. | Medium | Lazy relation loading now resolves local keys through the same field-path helper used by query/include code. | Mitigated |
| R-048 | P1 | Decorator and direct metadata relation APIs can bypass relation-name validation | Builder relation APIs validate names, but decorators and `modelMeta.relation()` could register reserved names directly. | Medium: reserved relation names can enter metadata from alternate public APIs. | Medium | Decorator and metadata-layer relation registration now validate names and relation paths centrally. | Mitigated |
| R-049 | P1 | Memory transaction commits can overwrite concurrent writes | The isolated memory transaction store validates optimistic locks only inside the transaction snapshot, not against parent state at commit time. Duplicate creates can also appear after the snapshot. | High: tests can miss stale-write or duplicate-create conflicts that production adapters would reject. | Medium | Memory transaction commit now rechecks duplicate creates and `expectedVersion` updates against parent state before applying dirty writes atomically. | Mitigated |
| R-050 | P1 | Cache key resolvers can run when no cache is available | Models with cache metadata but no registered cache adapter can still call the global `cacheKey` resolver during reads or transactional invalidation. | Medium: tenant/cache key resolvers with side effects or strict assumptions can fail even though caching is inactive. | Medium | Cache keys are now resolved only when a cache adapter is present; cache-disabled transactional writes skip cache invalidation entirely. | Mitigated |
| R-051 | P0 | `afterValidate` hooks can bypass write validation | `prepareWrite()` validated data, ran `afterValidate`, then cloned the hook result without validating it again. | High: a hook or plugin can unintentionally send schema-invalid data to stores. | Medium | `afterValidate` output is revalidated through the model validator before encoding or writing, with create/update regression coverage. | Mitigated |
| R-052 | P1 | Saved model instances can retain fields pruned by validation | `Model.save()` merged validated data back into the existing `data` object with `Object.assign`, leaving keys removed by validators on the live instance. | Medium: in-memory models can diverge from persisted rows and leak stale local fields into later logic. | Medium | `save()` now replaces the instance data shape with the validated write result and tests cover pruned-field cleanup. | Mitigated |
| R-053 | P1 | Search hooks can pass non-string queries to adapters | `beforeSearch` can replace the search query, but the core path validated options only and passed the mutated query directly to the search adapter. | Medium: custom adapters can crash or interpret unexpected query objects differently. | Medium | Search hook output is validated as a string before adapter routing/execution, with regression coverage that the adapter is not called on invalid queries. | Mitigated |
| R-054 | P1 | Static update patches can mutate models before safe-key checks | `Model.update()` merged the patch into a loaded model and relied on later save validation. Reserved or prototype keys can touch the live object first. | Medium: unsafe patches can cause local object pollution or extra adapter reads before rejection. | Medium | Update patches are cloned and checked for safe keys before any model load or merge, with reserved/prototype-key regression coverage. | Mitigated |
| R-055 | P1 | Text query operators can match missing fields by coercion | Memory/native filtering converted field values with `String(value)`, so a missing field could match `textContains: 'def'` through `"undefined"`. | Medium: test adapter results can include rows production backends would not match. | Medium | `textContains` and `startsWith` now require actual string operands and string field values before matching, with regression coverage for missing fields. | Mitigated |
| R-056 | P0 | Soft delete scopes can misclassify missing fields | `createSoftDeletePlugin()` scopes default reads with `deletedAt = null` and `onlyDeleted()` with `deletedAt != null`, while core equality treats missing `deletedAt` as `undefined`, not `null`. | High: legacy rows without the soft-delete field can disappear from normal reads and appear in deleted-only reads. | High | Added explicit `isNull`/`isNotNull` operators and moved soft-delete scopes onto them. Memory semantics treat missing as null for live reads and not deleted-only reads, with missing/null/timestamp coverage. | Mitigated |
| R-057 | P1 | Soft-delete helpers can ignore bound model context | `softDelete(model, id, context = getDefaultContext())` and `restore()` default to the global context even when passed a class returned by `Model.use(context)`. | High: helper calls can load or mutate rows through the wrong store in tests, multi-app runtimes, or request-scoped contexts. | Medium | `softDelete()` and `restore()` now resolve the bound model context when no explicit context is supplied, with distinct default/bound store regression coverage. | Mitigated |
| R-058 | P1 | Outbox search sync can conflict with default event payloads | `createOutboxPlugin()` includes row data only when `includeData` is true, but `runSearchSyncWorker()` requires `event.data` for index events. | High: default outbox configuration can repeatedly fail and requeue create/update search sync events. | Medium | `runSearchSyncWorker()` reloads the current row from the provided context when event data is absent, and deletes stale search docs when the row is gone. Legacy no-context mode still fails fast on missing data. | Mitigated |
| R-059 | P1 | Datastore query results expose cursors the adapter rejects | The Datastore adapter advertises `cursor: false` and rejects `plan.cursor`, but can still return Datastore `endCursor` in `QueryResult.cursor`. | Medium: users can receive a cursor from one query and fail when passing it to the next query on the same adapter. | Medium | Datastore no longer exposes native `endCursor` as portable `QueryResult.cursor` while `cursor: false`; tests assert `more` can be true without a reusable cursor. | Mitigated |
| R-060 | P2 | Custom store adapter capabilities are default-permissive | Built-in adapters declare capabilities, but a custom adapter that omits `capabilities` can still pass some planner checks for OR, cursor, select, and explicit containment operators. | Medium: third-party adapters can silently receive unsupported plans unless they know to opt out. | Medium | Missing store capabilities now default-deny optional query features and aggregate optimizations. Regression tests cover omitted capability matrices. | Mitigated |
| R-061 | P2 | Memory test seeding assumes `id` as the id field | `MemoryStoreAdapter.seed(modelName, rows)` keys rows by `row.id`, while active-ts models can use custom id fields such as `uid` or `slug`. | Medium: tests for custom-id models can seed rows under the wrong key and hide lookup failures. | Medium | `MemoryStoreAdapter.seed()` accepts resolved model metadata and uses its `idField`; `ActiveTestContext.seed()` now passes metadata, with custom-id regression coverage. | Mitigated |
| R-062 | P1 | Custom search adapter capabilities remain default-permissive | `assertSearchSupports()` returns early when `adapter.capabilities` is omitted, unlike store capability checks that now default-deny optional features. | High: third-party search adapters can silently receive unsupported `where`, `cursor`, or native search options. | Medium | Missing search capabilities now default-deny optional `where`, cursor, and native options, with regression coverage for omitted search capability matrices. | Mitigated |
| R-063 | P1 | Native search runtime checks still use false-only capability gates | `createNativeSearchAdapter()` advertises cursor support only when the store says `cursor: true`, but execution rejects cursor and multi-field OR only when underlying capabilities are explicitly `false`. | High: stores with partial capability declarations can receive unsupported cursor or OR plans through native search. | Medium | Native search runtime checks now require `store.capabilities.cursor === true` and `store.capabilities.or === true` when those features are used. | Mitigated |
| R-064 | P1 | Cloud document-store soft-delete null semantics may not include missing fields | The core soft-delete contract now treats missing fields as null, but Datastore and Firestore `isNull` are translated to backend null equality filters. Those backends may not match entities/documents where the field is absent. New soft-delete writes now materialize `deletedAt: null`, but legacy rows still require migration/backfill. | High: legacy Datastore/Firestore rows without `deletedAt` can still be excluded from live soft-delete queries. | Medium | Store capabilities now declare missing-field-null support; soft-delete live filters fail fast on adapters without that support unless `materializedNulls: true` is explicitly configured and documented. | Mitigated |
| R-065 | P2 | Test context seeding can break string-based custom seed helpers | `ActiveTestContext.seed()` now calls any store `seed` extension with `ResolvedModelMeta`; custom test stores that expose `seed(modelName: string, rows)` can receive an object key unexpectedly. | Medium: downstream test harnesses can break after adopting the new metadata-aware seed path. | Medium | Add a separate metadata-aware extension name such as `seedModel(meta, rows)`, or preserve `seed(name, rows)` and provide a compatibility fallback. | Mitigated |
| R-066 | P2 | Adapter contract suite capability gates do not match core default-deny semantics | `runStoreAdapterContract()` still treats `select !== false`, `aggregate !== false`, and `numericComparisons !== false` as support, while core now requires explicit `true` for optional features. | Medium: contract tests can exercise optional features on adapters that did not advertise them, or fail to catch missing capability declarations. | Medium | Contract feature gates now require explicit `true` for select, aggregate, and numeric comparison checks, aligning with core default-deny behavior. | Mitigated |
| R-067 | P1 | Null operators are not capability-gated for custom stores | `isNull` and `isNotNull` are now portable operators and can be injected by soft-delete scopes, but `assertStoreSupports()` has no capability check for them. | High: custom stores can receive unknown null operators even when optional features are otherwise default-denied. | Medium | Store capabilities now include `nullOperators`; `isNull` and `isNotNull` fail fast unless the adapter explicitly opts in. | Mitigated |
| R-068 | P1 | Runtime entity id inputs can bypass scalar and safe-number validation | `Model.create()` only rejects missing ids, and `entityIdKey()` accepts any non-number type by stringifying it. Public id paths such as create/find/update/delete can therefore accept objects, booleans, or unsafe numbers at runtime. | High: invalid ids can collide as strings such as `object:[object Object]`, reach adapters, or create rows that cannot be safely addressed later. | Medium | Centralize runtime id validation in the id codec and call it from create/find/update/delete/load/cache paths; require string ids or finite safe-integer numbers. | Mitigated |
| R-069 | P1 | Safe-data validation can miss non-plain object contents | `assertSafeDataKeys()` checks arrays and object keys but returns early for `Date`, `RegExp`, and `Uint8Array` and does not inspect `Map`, `Set`, or custom prototypes. | Medium: non-portable or nested unsafe data can pass memory/cache paths and later fail or serialize differently in database adapters. | Medium | Restrict persisted data to plain objects, arrays, and explicitly supported scalar/binary/date types, or deeply inspect/normalize Map/Set-like structures before adapter writes. | Mitigated |
| R-070 | P1 | Search-sync reloads payload-free events through cache-backed reads | `runSearchSyncWorker()` uses `context.loadById()` when event data is missing. That path can read from cache rather than the source store. | Medium: stale cache entries can cause search indexing to replay old data or delete a document when the store row exists. | Medium | Reload missing outbox payloads directly from the model's store adapter, bypassing entity cache and applying read validation/codecs explicitly. | Mitigated |
| R-071 | P2 | Memory search can match missing fields for empty queries | `MemorySearchAdapter.search()` coerces missing search fields to `''`, so an empty query can match rows that do not contain any declared search field. | Low to Medium: tests using empty search text can diverge from native or production search adapters. | Medium | Require a string field value before matching, mirroring `textContains`, or define/document empty-query semantics consistently across search adapters. | Mitigated |
| R-072 | P2 | CLI schema apply can be a no-op unless autoSync is configured | `active-ts schema apply` calls `context.schemaApply(models)`, and `schemaApply()` returns `[]` when `config.schema.autoSync` is absent or `off`. | Medium: users can run an explicit apply command and silently apply nothing unless their runtime context enables auto-sync. | Medium | Add an explicit apply mode parameter for CLI-driven applies, default CLI apply to safe mode, and make no-op applies visible in output. | Mitigated |
| R-073 | P2 | Search index schema hooks are not included in context schema plans | Search adapters expose `syncSchema()`, but `ActiveContext.schemaPlan()` and `schemaApply()` only group models by store and call store schema hooks. | Medium: Algolia/Elasticsearch index changes can be omitted from `schema diff/generate/apply`. | Medium | Extend schema planning to group models by search adapter and include `SearchAdapter.syncSchema()` plans alongside store schema plans. | Mitigated |
| R-074 | P1 | Relation key values are not validated as portable scalars | `LazyRef.loadNow()` can cast a local relation value to `EntityId`, and batched `preloadIncludes()` uses raw local/foreign values in `Set`, `Map`, and `in` queries without validating their runtime shape. | High: object, array, Date, or unsafe numeric relation keys can silently fail in memory, be rejected differently by adapters, or bypass the typed id codec on id-backed relations. | Medium | Validate relation local/foreign values before loading: id-backed one relations should require a valid `EntityId`, and foreign-key relation queries should require portable scalar comparable values. Add batch and direct lazy-load regressions. | Mitigated |

| R-100 | P1 | Deferred transaction cache invalidation failures leave stale cache | In a transaction, `context.invalidate()` queues `performInvalidate()` as an afterCommit task. `runDeferredTasks()` catches afterCommit errors, logs a warning, and continues. | High: a committed write can leave positive or negative cache entries stale with no retry path. | Medium | Deferred cache invalidation failures now reject the transaction after commit via `AggregateError`, with tests proving the store write committed and the caller is notified. | Mitigated |

| R-119 | P2 | Optional peer dependency ranges are unconstrained | `package.json` declares backend SDK peers such as `pg`, `mongodb`, `redis`, `algoliasearch`, and Google SDKs as `"*"`. | Medium: a future major SDK release can satisfy peer resolution while breaking adapter runtime assumptions. | Medium | Optional peer dependencies now declare supported major ranges and adapter docs include the compatibility matrix for backend SDK installation. | Mitigated |

| R-122 | P2 | Published declaration and source maps point to unpacked source files | The tarball includes `build/src/**/*.d.ts.map` and `*.js.map`, whose `sources` entries point back to `src/**/*.ts`, but the `files` list publishes `build/src` and docs, not `src`. | Low to Medium: IDE "go to source" and debugging can land on missing files in installed packages. | Medium | The package now includes `src` alongside `build/src`, and pack smoke verifies installed source files exist for emitted declaration/source maps. | Mitigated |
| R-123 | P2 | Node type declarations can exceed the documented runtime baseline | The package requires Node `>=22`, but dev dependencies use `@types/node` `^25.0.0`. | Medium: code can typecheck against Node 25 APIs that are unavailable on the documented Node 22 baseline unless exercised directly in tests. | Low to Medium | `@types/node` is now pinned to the Node 22 major, matching the documented `engines.node >=22` baseline. | Mitigated |

| R-128 | P2 | Projection typing does not distinguish partial model instances | `select()` returns the same `QueryBuilder<TModel>` and `load()`/`first()` expose full `TModel` instances, even though runtime marks selected rows as partial and blocks full-model operations. | Medium: callers can typecheck calls to fields or operations that will be missing or fail at runtime on partial instances. | Medium | `select()` now returns `QueryBuilder<PartialModel<...>>`, selected fields are required while non-selected fields are optional, blocked full-model operations are typed as unavailable, and compile-time regressions cover the contract. | Mitigated |
| R-129 | P2 | Batch loads are unbounded | `BatchLoader` flushes every pending id in the same microtask as one `loadManyNow()` call, and `loadManyNow()` forwards the whole id set to cache `getMany()` and store `getMany()` without chunking. | Medium: large request fan-out can exceed Redis/SDK request limits or create high-latency single calls. | Medium | Contexts now support `batch.maxSize` with a default of 500; both pending batch flushes and direct `loadManyNow()` calls chunk large id sets before cache/store reads, with regression coverage. | Mitigated |
| R-130 | P2 | Aggregate fallback can full-scan through `query()` | When a store lacks native `aggregate()` support, `QueryBuilder.runAggregate()` falls back to `store.query()` with filters but no limit, then computes aggregates in memory. | Medium to High: count/sum helpers can accidentally load large collections from adapters that cannot aggregate natively. | Medium | Aggregate query fallback is now disabled by default and requires explicit `aggregate.allowQueryFallback: true`; unsupported adapters fail fast instead of full-scanning silently. | Mitigated |

A patched global descriptor function could make a raw adapter appear context-bound, including making an unregistered native-search backing store look registered during transaction rebinding. | High: extension boundaries and native search transaction routing could be bypassed in hostile-intrinsic environments. | Low to Medium | Context-bound marker reads now use captured Object descriptor intrinsics. Regression coverage verifies raw adapter guards and unregistered native search transaction rebinding ignore forged descriptors. | Mitigated |
| R-1613 | P1 | Untrusted Datastore entity-key markers could override payload scope | Shared Datastore query-result normalization parsed any non-enumerable `ACTIVE_TS_ENTITY_KEY`, even from stores that did not carry the Datastore trust marker. A custom store could attach a forged key inside the requested ancestor while returning payload fields for a sibling ancestor. | High: direct reads, middleware queries, and aggregate fallback could accept out-of-scope Datastore rows from untrusted adapters. | Low to Medium | Entity-key markers influence scoped row identity only when the store is explicitly marked as trusting Datastore entity-key rows; untrusted markers fall back to payload ancestor validation. Regression coverage exercises direct get/getMany, middleware query, and aggregate fallback. | Mitigated |
| R-1614 | P1 | Route-dependent outbox sync skipped explicit adapter-tagged search indexes | Search schema planning includes explicit `searchIndex.adapter` routes in addition to `schemaSearchAdapters`, but `runSearchSyncWorker()` route fan-out only iterated schema routes. A store-backed event could be acknowledged after updating route-dependent backends while leaving an explicit adapter index stale. | High: search sync can silently miss declared indexes in applications mixing route-dependent search with explicit adapter-tagged indexes. | Low to Medium | Search sync route resolution now merges explicit adapter-tagged index routes with schema route candidates before indexing. Regression coverage verifies `short`, `long`, and `explicit` adapters all receive the document before ack. | Mitigated |
| R-1615 | P1 | Direct search schema handles skipped alias-tagged indexes | Top-level schema planning rewrote search index metadata for the registered adapter kind, but `context.searchAdapter('alias').schema.plan/apply()` and `syncSchema()` passed raw metadata to the retained adapter. Built-in adapters such as Algolia then filtered `adapter: 'alias'` indexes against their physical kind and emitted empty direct schema plans. | High: users can validate top-level schema plans successfully while low-level schema handles used by tools or migrations silently omit declared search indexes. | Low to Medium | Context-bound search schema handles now normalize models with the route alias and retained adapter index kind before invoking schema hooks, matching search/index/delete behavior. Regression coverage verifies direct Algolia plan/apply/syncSchema include alias-tagged indexes. | Mitigated |
| R-1616 | P1 | Namespaced Datastore trusted keys could split one row identity | Trusted Datastore query rows with namespace-less entity-key markers were accepted inside adapter-namespaced scopes, but duplicate detection used the marker ancestor as-is. A namespace-less marker and a tenant-namespaced marker for the same entity could therefore produce different internal identities during selected queries or aggregate fallback. | High: projected Datastore reads and fallback aggregates can return or count the same physical tenant row twice when wrappers preserve SDK-style keys without namespace metadata. | Low to Medium | Trusted scoped entity-key ancestors now inherit the scoped adapter namespace for internal identity while still rejecting out-of-scope explicit namespaces. Regression coverage verifies namespace-less and namespaced selected rows under the same tenant scope are detected as duplicates, and retained transaction namespace propagation still accepts single namespace-less SDK keys. | Mitigated |
| R-1617 | P1 | Namespaced Datastore search identities could drop namespace-less SDK keys | `withDatastoreSearchNamespace()` applied adapter namespaces through the payload ancestor resolver, but `searchDocumentIdentity()` trusted namespace-less entity-key markers before the payload path. Native or direct search indexing over projected Datastore rows could therefore compute namespace-less document identities, or reject them as mismatched when adapters snapshotted namespaced model metadata. | High: tenant search indexes can collide or reject valid Datastore rows when SDK-style keys omit namespace metadata while the wrapped store carries `datastoreNamespace`. | Low to Medium | Datastore search namespace metadata is now attached to the ancestor wrapper function so adapter model snapshots retain it, and entity-key-derived search identities inherit that namespace before comparison and hashing. Regression coverage verifies native search hits from namespace-less SDK keys use the wrapped store namespace. | Mitigated |
| R-1618 | P1 | Physical search index kind tags were not routed through registered aliases | Top-level schema planning and outbox route discovery treated an explicit `searchIndex.adapter` value as a registered route name. If an adapter was registered as `primary` with `searchIndexKind: 'algolia'`, an index tagged `adapter: 'algolia'` worked through direct handles but `schemaPlan()` and outbox sync attempted to route to an unregistered `algolia` adapter. | High: applications wrapping remote search adapters behind stable route aliases can silently skip schema/outbox coverage or fail at deployment/runtime. | Low to Medium | Search schema route discovery now maps physical index-kind tags back through declared schema route candidates when no literal route is registered, and outbox fan-out treats route names and index kinds as covered routes. Regression coverage verifies schema planning and outbox sync route physical `algolia` indexes through a `primary` alias. | Mitigated |
| R-1619 | P1 | Unscoped namespaced Datastore trusted keys could split identities | R-1616 covered scoped ancestor queries, but unscoped namespaced queries still used namespace-less trusted entity-key ancestors as-is. A namespaced adapter could return the same physical row once with a namespace-less SDK key and once with an explicit tenant key, and duplicate detection would accept both. | High: tenant-wide Datastore scans and aggregate fallbacks can double-count or return duplicate physical rows when wrappers preserve mixed SDK key metadata. | Low to Medium | Trusted entity-key ancestors now inherit the adapter namespace even when no scoped ancestor was requested, while mismatched explicit namespaces are rejected. Regression coverage verifies unscoped selected queries detect namespace-less and namespaced keys for the same tenant row as duplicates. | Mitigated |
| R-1620 | P1 | Dataful Datastore outbox deletes ignored stored identity metadata | `runSearchSyncWorker()` accepted delete events with payload data, but `outboxEventSearchDocumentIdentity()` derived the Datastore ancestor only from payload ancestor fields. A delete event that already carried `modelDatastoreAncestor` or a preserved SDK entity-key marker could fail, or delete the wrong document identity, when the data payload omitted ancestor fields. | High: dataful outbox deletes are common for audit/retry flows, and missing projected ancestor fields could leave stale tenant search documents after the event is acknowledged. | Low to Medium | Dataful outbox delete identity resolution now uses preserved `ACTIVE_TS_ENTITY_KEY` metadata and falls back to stored event `modelDatastoreAncestor` while still rejecting mismatches. Regression coverage verifies metadata-backed and entity-key-backed dataful deletes remove the correct Datastore search documents. | Mitigated |
| R-1621 | P1 | Physical search index aliases outside schema candidates were undiscovered | The physical-kind alias fix in R-1618 only searched `queryPlanner.schemaSearchAdapters` candidates. If an explicit index was tagged `adapter: 'algolia'` but the actual registered alias `primary` was outside that candidate list, schema planning and outbox route discovery still tried the unregistered physical name. | High: mixed route-dependent search configurations can keep physical remote adapters outside normal schema candidates, causing deploy-time schema failures or missed outbox indexing. | Low to Medium | Search schema route discovery now falls back to all registered search routes when mapping physical index kinds, while still adding only routes whose `searchIndexKind` matches. Regression coverage verifies a `primary` Algolia alias outside `schemaSearchAdapters` is discovered for schema planning and outbox sync. | Mitigated |
| R-1622 | P1 | Explicit outbox physical adapter overrides bypassed registered source validation | `runSearchSyncWorker({ adapter: 'algolia', context, search })` treated an unregistered physical adapter name as valid when the provided search adapter advertised the same physical kind. In a context that registered the real adapter under an alias such as `primary`, a spoofed adapter with `searchIndexKind: 'algolia'` could receive index/delete calls without matching the registered source chain. | High: low-level outbox workers can be wired with explicit adapter overrides during migrations, and source validation must prevent writes to unregistered or spoofed search backends. | Low to Medium | Explicit physical adapter overrides now resolve through registered schema routes when possible and require the provided adapter source to match the registered alias before executing. Regression coverage verifies spoofed physical-kind adapters are rejected before delete calls. | Mitigated |
| R-1624 | P1 | Explicit outbox search overrides could execute an unregistered wrapper source | Source-chain validation allowed a provided middleware wrapper to match a registered raw search adapter, and explicit single-route execution returned the provided wrapper when the registered adapter had no source marker. An unregistered wrapper could therefore drop or alter `index`/`delete` calls while the worker still acknowledged the event for a named route. | High: migration workers can pass context plus explicit search handles; executing unregistered middleware for a named adapter route breaks the guarantee that outbox delivery targets the registered backend graph. | Low to Medium | Explicit search sync route resolution now executes the registered adapter after source-chain validation, while the no-override worker path continues to support deliberate low-level wrapper injection. Regression coverage verifies an explicit provided wrapper over the registered raw adapter is not called and the registered memory index receives the document. | Mitigated |
| R-1626 | P1 | Store outbox leases split canonical Datastore identities | StoreOutbox lease ordering keyed ancestor-only events by raw ancestor/id and identity-only events by `modelIdentity`. Equivalent Datastore events could therefore be leased together when one row carried only a canonical search identity and a later row carried only ancestor metadata; namespace-less ancestors also failed to inherit the store namespace. | High: persisted outbox rows from mixed versions or import tools can interleave same-entity Datastore events and violate per-entity ordering under tenant namespaces. | Low to Medium | StoreOutbox lease ordering now canonicalizes ancestor/id rows through `datastoreSearchDocumentIdentity()` with the store namespace, matching identity-only rows. Regression coverage verifies identity-only and inherited-namespace ancestor events block each other while sibling ancestors can proceed. | Mitigated |

## Completed Remediation Plan

1. P0 correctness pass

   `Model.use(context)`, negative cache invalidation, relation foreign key
   behavior, `SearchBuilder.where()`, and adapter query semantics are covered by
   code paths that either behave consistently or fail fast.

2. Contract stabilization

   Adapter contracts now exercise the common operator, projection, aggregate,
   cursor, and id-codec behavior that each adapter advertises.

3. Concurrency and metadata lifecycle

   Transactions run in child contexts and metadata resolution is versioned so
   late metadata attachment invalidates cached resolution.

4. Production maturity

   Outbox-backed search sync with requeue-on-failure, standardized cursor
   handling, duplicate-create conflict semantics, soft delete, optimistic
   locking, schema CLI, cache hardening, validation adapters, license, CI, and
   security reporting are implemented or explicitly capability-gated.

5. Hook, transaction, and adapter hardening

   Transaction cache reads are coherent after in-transaction writes, unsupported
   and cross-store transaction writes fail fast, hook-mutated plans are
   revalidated before adapter execution and after validation hooks, relation
   metadata names are validated, search hook queries are type-checked before
   adapter execution, static update patches are safe-key checked before merge,
   model instances adopt the validated post-save shape, text operators avoid
   missing-field coercion, hook-mutated where predicates require own fields,
   and adapter-specific cursor/index edge cases are covered by
   regressions.

## Recent Remediation Plan

1. Soft-delete semantics

   Soft-delete now uses explicit null operators, and memory/query tests cover
   missing, explicit null, and timestamp rows.

2. Context-bound helpers

   `softDelete()` and `restore()` resolve a bound model context when no
   explicit context is supplied.

3. Outbox and cursor contracts

   Search sync can reload data for payload-free outbox events, and Datastore
   keeps native cursors out of portable `QueryResult.cursor`.

4. Adapter and testing ergonomics

   Custom adapter capability omission now fails closed for optional features,
   and memory/test seeding is metadata-aware for custom id fields.

## Review Cadence

- Review P0 risks before each feature release.
- Re-score this register whenever adapter behavior changes.
- Promote mitigated items only after tests or documentation make the behavior
  enforceable.
